    "displayName": "https://dev.azure.com/smallcorp/Infrastructure/_wiki/wikis/Infra-Code-Wiki/4865/CrossRegion-Backup-API-Reference-for-Backup-and-Restore-Procedures-Data-Retention-Policies-and-Recovery-Testing",

      "parsedData": "## Overview\nOur cross‑region backup workflow relies on API‑driven snapshot replication across West Europe and North Europe, designed to handle high‑throughput AI inference data while meeting **CISO‑mandated retention tiers** established in December 2025. The replication engine (`replicatord`) was upgraded in v2.8.4 to reduce regional transfer latency by an average of 34 ms during off‑peak windows. This page documents the internal APIs we expose for initiating, monitoring, and validating cross‑region backups, plus the retention and recovery‑testing procedures that ensure compliance with our R3 risk tolerance classification.  \nA structural change introduced last year requires rate‑limiting callers: at **>500 concurrent connections, the connection pool starts rejecting** non‑priority backup sessions. This is intentional to prevent a re‑occurrence of the April 2025 incident where exhausted pools delayed restore tests by nearly 40 minutes.\n\n![Cross-region backup flow](/.attachments/cross-region-backup-flow.png)\n\n### Non-Obvious Behavior  \nThe most unexpected finding during the 2025 Q4 review was that shrinking snapshot chunk size from 256 MB to 192 MB *increased* throughput by 11%. The network behaved more predictably under transient congestion, reducing jitter that previously created erratic replication windows.\n\n## Authentication\nAll API endpoints require **HMAC-SHA256** signatures generated from the service principal `svc-backup-north-eu`. The signing key rotates every 14 days, and rotation failures are logged as high‑signal events in Sentinel with the tag `backup-auth-rot-fail`.  \nBefore generating signatures, clients must cache the region‑specific nonce retrieved from `GET /v1/regions/{region}/nonce`. The nonce is valid for 45 seconds; using an expired value triggers a security exception flagged as R2 severity.  \nWe enforce strict time drift limits: clients drifting more than ±20 seconds from UTC are rejected. This safeguard was introduced after we detected three misconfigured AKS nodes in October 2025 that produced invalid signatures causing a false failover.\n\n### CLI Example\n```\n# Fetch region nonce\ncurl -s -H \"X-Client: infra-tools\" \\\n  [link](https://api.smallcorp.net/v1/regions/weu/nonce)\n\n# Trigger snapshot backup\ncurl -X POST [link](https://api.smallcorp.net/v1/backup/start) \\\n  -H \"X-Auth: <hmac-value>\" \\\n  -d '{\"dataset\":\"ai-metrics\",\"mode\":\"cross-region\"}'\n```\n\n## Endpoints\nEvery endpoint below was hardened in v2.8.4 to apply uniform retry semantics with an exponential pattern capped at three attempts. We validated that retries above this threshold increased tail latency rather than reducing it.\n\n### ### Backup Initiation\nThis endpoint initiates a region‑to‑region snapshot. It enforces a strict payload schema to avoid ambiguity in retention classification.\n\n- **POST `/v1/backup/start`** – initiates a cross‑region snapshot and returns a job ID; rejects any dataset not registered in the replication catalog.  \n- **POST `/v1/backup/cancel`** – attempts cancellation, though completion is not guaranteed once replication exceeds 70% of transfer volume.  \n- **GET `/v1/backup/{jobId}/status`** – returns the current stage plus cryptographic integrity markers computed per 4 GB segment.\n\n### ### Restore Procedures\nCross‑region restore operations prioritize recovery integrity over speed, using double‑verification of SHA‑512 digests.\n\n- **POST `/v1/restore/start`** – launches a restore workflow that must run in an isolated recovery namespace.  \n- **GET `/v1/restore/{jobId}/logs`** – streams restore logs; we cap log messages at 5,000 entries to avoid log‑processing stalls.  \n- **POST `/v1/restore/commit`** – finalizes restored data into the destination dataset once consistency markers pass.\n\n## Data Retention Policies\nRetention requirements differ between inference logs, model artifacts, and experiment metadata. Our December 2025 control update mandates separate retention tiers per data class, each enforced by background workers in the `retentiond` service.  \nA counterintuitive discovery emerged during load tests: longer retention windows for experiment metadata did **not** increase storage costs proportionally. Deduplication across runs reduced effective volume by 27%, allowing us to maintain a 120‑day window without new capacity purchases.\n\n### ### Retention Tiers\n- **Tier A – 180 days**: high‑value operational metrics with mandatory multi‑region replication.  \n- **Tier B – 120 days**: AI experiment metadata stored with aggressive deduplication.  \n- **Tier C – 35 days**: transient datasets primarily used during model rollout and validation.\n\n## Recovery Testing\nWe run recovery tests monthly using the `restore-lab-north-eu` sandbox. These are automated through our Azure DevOps pipeline `Restore-Validation-CI` that validates replication consistency, checks that snapshot lineage records match expected digests, and confirms that job orchestration did not exceed the defined 25‑minute test SLA.  \nDuring the March 2026 test cycle, we discovered that restore time improved by removing local caching of checksum manifests. Disk I/O contention on the test cluster caused caching to degrade performance rather than improve it, cutting restore times from 31 minutes down to 22 minutes when disabled.\n\n### ### Validation Steps\n1. Trigger a controlled backup of the `ai-metrics` dataset using `POST /v1/backup/start`.  \n2. Use `restore-lab-north-eu` to initiate a test restore.  \n3. Compare integrity manifests with `tools/check-integrity --dataset ai-metrics-lab`.  \n\n### ### API Monitoring\nTo detect drift or latent failures, monitoring thresholds include:  \n- **Replication lag > 900 seconds** – triggers a region health warning.  \n- **Restore throughput < 350 MB/s** – indicates network or disk contention.  \n- **Missing lineage markers** – treated as a security‑critical anomaly and escalated to the on‑call security specialist.",

Deduplication across runs reduced effective volume by 27%, allowing us to maintain a 120‑day window without new capacity purchases.\n\n### ### Retention Tiers\n- **Tier A – 180 days**: high‑value operational metrics with mandatory multi‑region replication.  \n- **Tier B – 120 days**: AI experiment metadata stored with aggressive deduplication.  \n- **Tier C – 35 days**: transient datasets primarily used during model rollout and validation.\n\n## Recovery Testing\nWe run recovery tests monthly using the `restore-lab-north-eu` sandbox. These are automated through our Azure DevOps pipeline `Restore-Validation-CI` that validates replication consistency, checks that snapshot lineage records match expected digests, and confirms that job orchestration did not exceed the defined 25‑minute test SLA.  \nDuring the March 2026 test cycle, we discovered that restore time improved by removing local caching of checksum manifests. Disk I/O contention on the test cluster caused caching to degrade performance rather than improve it, cutting restore times from 31 minutes down to 22 minutes when disabled.\n\n### ### Validation Steps\n1. Trigger a controlled backup of the `ai-metrics` dataset using `POST /v1/backup/start`.  \n2. Use `restore-lab-north-eu` to initiate a test restore.  \n3. Compare integrity manifests with `tools/check-integrity --dataset ai-metrics-lab`.  \n\n### ### API Monitoring\nTo detect drift or latent failures, monitoring thresholds include:  \n- **Replication lag > 900 seconds** – triggers a region health warning.  \n- **Restore throughput < 350 MB/s** – indicates network or disk contention.  \n- **Missing lineage markers** – treated as a security‑critical anomaly and escalated to the on‑call security specialist.",
